content.text: Mentiroso (Spanish for 'Liar') is the Hispanic world's definitive version of the global bluffing game 'Cheat' or 'I Doubt It'. Played with the 40-card Spanish deck, it is a game of shedding and deception. Players discard cards face-down and claim their rank; if an opponent believes the player is lying, they shout 'Â¡Mentiroso!'. It is a cultural staple in Spain and Latin America, often played in families to teach social observation and poker-face maintenance.
Dates back centuries as a gambling folk game. The Spanish version is distinct due to the use of the 40-card deck (Oros, Copas, Espadas, Bastos).

Two to six players; the game is often best with four. The entire 40-card Spanish deck is dealt out evenly so that each player has the same number of cards (or at most one card difference). Players should keep their card count visible.
The entire deck is dealt out evenly.
